real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to clearly composed photos of road and rail vehicles (buses, trucks, vans, cars, locomotives) in which one vehicle is the main subject. It is more active on these than on scenes with no single main subject, and it tends to prefer sharp, level, well-framed subjects. The apparent preference for vehicles facing right did not replicate on new photos: right versus left and right versus head-on both fell to ordinary percentiles. The single-subject effect (row 5) did replicate, but similar units show it too, so it is largely shared rather than particular to this unit.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to road and rail vehicles (buses, trucks, vans, cars, locomotives) shown as a single, clear, sharp main subject. It is weaker on photos with no clear facing direction or no single main subject. The apparent right-facing preference did not hold up: on new photos, right-facing vehicles were not more active than left-facing or head-on/away ones (rows 1 and 4 failed). Only the contrast between a right-facing subject and no clear direction or no single subject replicated (row 5, percentile 99). That likely reflects a general preference for a well-defined vehicle subject rather than direction, and similar unit 1 partly shares it. The preferences for sharp, level, well-framed subjects are mostly shared with similar units, so they are not particular to this unit.

real_s3.explanation: This unit responds to vehicles such as buses, trucks, vans and locomotives, and is most active when the photo shows one clearly oriented vehicle rather than a scene with no single subject or no clear facing direction. The strong right-over-left and right-over-head-on preference in the first sample did not replicate on new photos (row 1 percentile 17, row 4 percentile 46), so it was likely noise. What held is that right-facing subjects beat directionless or subject-less photos (row 5, percentile 99). Similar unit 1 shares that preference partly, so it is only somewhat particular to this unit. The preference for sharp, level, well-framed subjects is largely shared with similar units.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (buses, trucks, cars, locomotives and similar) whose front faces or points to the right of the frame. On both the original and new photos it is clearly more active for right-facing vehicles than for left-facing ones or for head-on and rear views. The edge over photos with no clear facing direction did not hold on new photos, so the preference is specifically right versus other definite orientations. Preferences for sharp, level, well-framed subjects are shared with similar units and are not particular to this one.

null_s2.explanation: Among vehicle classes (buses, trucks, vans, cars, locomotives), this unit fires more when the vehicle faces or points to the right. It is more active for right-facing vehicles than for left-facing ones and than for vehicles seen head-on or from behind, and both differences held on new photos. Its edge over photos with no clear direction or no single subject did not replicate, since that group was small (11 photos) and the sign flipped. Its weaker preferences for sharp, level, well-framed subjects are largely shared with similar units, so they are not particular to this one.

null_s3.explanation: Among vehicle classes (buses, trucks, vans, locomotives and similar), this unit is more active when the main subject faces or points to the right. It responds more to right-facing views than to left-facing views, and more than to head-on or rear views. This direction preference held on new photos. The comparison of right-facing against directionless or no-single-subject photos did not hold. Preferences for sharp, level, well-framed subjects are weaker and largely shared with similar units.
